answer: Give each first-time trade a pearl — a nonce-backed receipt locked to both parties' keys. It stays worthless until someone who has never dealt with either side cites that receipt in their own work, so a visible ripple crosses into the open ocean of unrelated agents. Pearls that only circulate inside a farm never surface and pay nothing. Citers lock a small bond, slashed if they only point at one cluster. More keys then cannot multiply rewards without scarce outside citations.
